channel.title: Security Brief
channel.description: Original analysis and ranked cybersecurity news with links to original sources

item.title: The edge is where attackers get in: this week's firewall, VPN and remote-access exploits
item.description: Five exploited flaws in firewalls, VPNs, remote-support software and file-sharing servers show one pattern. The systems that sit at the edge of your network, and that administrators manage remotely, are the weakest link. Here is what to check first.

item.title: October 2026 Patch Tuesday: what the Microsoft feed shows and what to do
item.description: The Microsoft feed lists few entries, and most of them are updates to October's release rather than new fixes. The one item that needs planning is a .NET remote code execution flaw that Microsoft has not fixed yet. Identity Web and WSL need version checks if you use them.

item.title: Weekly M365 & Entra Briefing: 13 to 19 October 2026
item.description: Exchange sign-in problems after October Windows Server updates, an identity-based incident at ConnectWise that affected Microsoft 365 tenants, and why device-code abuse is still worth a Conditional Access check.

item.title: Critical Juniper Session Smart Conductor Flaw Exploited in Attacks
item.description: Tracked as CVE-2026-103406, the vulnerability allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root. The post Critical Juniper Session Smart Conductor Flaw Exploited in Attacks appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Drupal warns of new site takeover flaw exploited in attacks
item.description: The Drupal security team says attackers are exploiting a second critical vulnerability that lets them breach and hijack unpatched websites.

item.title: Hackers Exploit Critical ScreenConnect Flaw to Hijack MSP Technician PCs Without Warning
item.description: Threat actors are exploiting a now-patched security flaw in ConnectWise ScreenConnect to target managed service provider (MSP) servers. item.title: SAP NetWeaver, Cisco Expressway Flaws Exploited in Attacks
item.description: Threat actors could exploit them to leak or modify server information and to execute commands as root. The post SAP NetWeaver, Cisco Expressway Flaws Exploited in Attacks appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Switzerland Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Breached Critical Infrastructure Operators
item.description: Attackers using AI agents have broken into computer systems at Swiss organizations in four of five confirmed attacks, the first such cases in the country, the country's cybersecurity agency said yesterday. Three of the attacks targeted critical infrastructure operators, and two of those succeeded, with no major…

item.title: Hackers now exploit critical Drupal RCE flaw to hijack sites
item.description: The Drupal security team has confirmed that a critical vulnerability that lets attackers hijack unpatched sites has been actively exploited since at least Thursday.

item.title: US Air Force cloud platform reportedly hacked in latest federal breach
item.description: Hackers have reportedly breached the US Air Force's Cloud One computing platform, adding to a recent wave of cyberattacks affecting US government agencies, including the FBI, CIA, and Treasury Department.

item.title: Software giant SAP confirms cyber incident amid reports of source code breach
item.description: German software giant SAP confirmed a cybersecurity incident following reports that hackers infiltrated its software development infrastructure, potentially gaining access to the company’s source code.

item.title: In Other News: Tanker Cyberattacks, EU Quantum Act, New VirusTotal Capabilities
item.description: Noteworthy stories that might have slipped under the radar: RansomwareHelp accused of profiting from ransom payments, USDA payment systems breach, cybersecurity firm Radware hacked. The post In Other News: Tanker Cyberattacks, EU Quantum Act, New VirusTotal Capabilities appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Microsoft: China’s Salt Typhoon hackers are using Artex
item.description: An AI tool implicated in several high-profile breaches is rapidly being integrated into the hacking suites of groups from China and North Korea, Microsoft said.

item.title: Hackers Exploit Unpatched Flaw in Defunct Idunno AntiCsrf Library
item.description: Attackers can exploit CVE-2026-131914 to achieve remote code execution via a single web request containing specially crafted data. The post Hackers Exploit Unpatched Flaw in Defunct Idunno AntiCsrf Library appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: New Boston Scientific data breach exposes personal, medical info
item.description: Medical technology company Boston Scientific is sending data breach notices to individuals affected by a cyberattack on the firm.

item.title: Your Firewall Isn't Enough: The Hidden Risk of Unmanaged VMs
item.description: Forgotten virtual machines, unpatched servers, and excessive access permissions can create security blind spots across IT infrastructure. ISPsystem explains how centralized infrastructure management, access controls, and resource lifecycle automation can help reduce these risks.

item.title: Japan’s education ministry discloses breach of government procurement system
item.description: Japan’s education ministry disclosed earlier this week that hackers breached its government procurement system, potentially exposing records containing business information and email addresses.

item.title: 1Password Hacked, Customer Data and Source Code Stolen in GitHub Account Breach
item.description: Popular password management software 1Password on Wednesday disclosed a security incident involving its backend systems that led to the unauthorized access of some customer information, but emphasized that customer password vaults and other secrets were not accessed. item.title: ShinyHunters Claims Comeback, New Inception Group Rejects Alleged Ties
item.description: An account tied to ShinyHunters announced the group’s return, as Okta spots possible links between Inception and ShinyHunters hackers. The post ShinyHunters Claims Comeback, New Inception Group Rejects Alleged Ties appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Drupal Flaw Found by Anthropic Scanner Exploited in Attacks
item.description: CISA has added the vulnerability to its KEV catalog and instructed federal agencies to patch it within three days. The post Drupal Flaw Found by Anthropic Scanner Exploited in Attacks appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Hackers reportedly breached CIA intelligence analysis system
item.description: Unknown attackers have reportedly breached an open-source intelligence analysis system at the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA)

item.title: Iran-Aligned Volant Manticore Uses IPFS-Based KuboShell Backdoor in Espionage Campaigns
item.description: A previously undocumented Iran-aligned cyber espionage group called Volant Manticore has targeted telecommunications companies, airlines, and critical infrastructure in Cyprus. Central to the group's operations is a backdoor called KuboShell that uses the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) for command-and-control (C2)…

item.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health flaw exploited to steal tenant data
item.description: Microsoft is warning organizations that it suffered a data breach after attackers exploited a vulnerability in its Entra Connect Health service to gain unauthorized access to administrator email addresses and tenant configuration information.

item.title: pCloud Password Manager Hit by Cyber Attack Involving Email Address Exposure and Login Attempts
item.description: Cross-platform password manager pCloud Pass has confirmed it was targeted by a cyber attack after users reported seeing unknown devices being connected to their accounts. item.title: pCloud confirms password manager hack after suspicious login alerts
item.description: The pCloud Pass password manager suffered a cyberattack, with users reporting that unknown devices had connected to their accounts even with two-factor authentication (2FA) enabled.

item.title: Matters.AI Lands India’s Largest Cybersecurity Pre-Series A Round to Fight AI Data Risks
item.description: The security startup consolidates four legacy security tools into an autonomous platform that uses context-aware AI to trace sensitive data lineage, analyze user intent, and automatically remediate threats across enterprise environments.

item.title: Malwarebytes Antivirus: Get 50% off during Black Friday 2026
item.description: Malwarebytes' 2026 Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale is now live, offering 50% off security subscriptions for individuals, families, and small businesses, including its antivirus software, VPN, identity theft protection, and personal data removal services.

item.description: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a cyber attack in which a threat actor leveraged a Microsoft Store application to deliver a remote access trojan (RAT) called Vinci RAT. item.title: Microsoft removes WSUS server role in Windows Server 2028
item.description: Microsoft will remove the WSUS server role from Windows Server 2028, the next major release of its server operating system.

item.title: 100,000 Potentially Impacted by Colorado Data Breach
item.description: Hackers breached the digital identification and document storage application myColorado and accessed user-uploaded data. The post 100,000 Potentially Impacted by Colorado Data Breach appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Microsoft pushes emergency hotpatch to fix Windows Server crashes
item.description: Microsoft has released an emergency hotpatch update to address Windows Server 2025 crashes triggered after installing this month's security hotpatch update (KB5131077).

item.title: New NFS2ROOT Linux flaw can let attackers gain root privileges
item.description: ​A 12-year-old critical vulnerability in the Linux kernel's Network File System (NFS) server, tracked as CVE-2026-99362, allows remote attackers to gain root privileges.

item.title: Hex Package Manager Warns of Potential Data Breach
item.description: A vulnerability in hex.pm allowed hackers to run commands on web servers. No evidence of data modification was found, but database reads are not logged. The post Hex Package Manager Warns of Potential Data Breach appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Italy and Switzerland warn of autonomous AI-driven cyberattacks
item.description: Swiss and Italian cybersecurity agencies are warning about automated cyberattacks powered by AI agents targeting organizations in the critical infrastructure sector.

item.description: An unknown threat actor has been using artificial intelligence (AI)-driven offensive tooling in a campaign targeting Check Point Security Management servers, impacting 22 distinct organizations across the world. item.title: Rackspace shuts down Spot cloud platform after security breach
item.description: Rackspace is shutting down its Rackspace Spot cloud platform after a security breach allowed hackers to access customer Kubernetes clusters and secrets, giving customers until December 8 to migrate their services and download their data.

item.title: Radware discloses breach exposing customer cloud access keys
item.description: Cybersecurity company Radware says attackers gained access to some of its customers' account details and cloud access keys through an unsecured internal Cloud WAF (Web Application Firewall) management API that was left exposed online.
